claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your living situation better.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to check a few more details about your circumstances to ensure you meet all the eligibility requirements.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?** (I'm asking this because eligibility depends on your residency and immigration status.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Before I make a final assessment, let me check the specific rules about this situation by reviewing the official eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see from the eligibility rules that there are specific provisions for living abroad. Let me ask you a clarifying question:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as working for the UK government or in the diplomatic service), or are you living in one of the specific countries where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad as a regular person.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now make an assessment.

According to the UK government's Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. 

The rules do allow for exceptions if you're a Crown servant or living in certain specific countries, but as you've indicated, neither of those apply to your situation.

Since you're living abroad as a regular person and not falling into any of the specific exceptions, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under the current rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

The key reason is that Child Benefit eligibility requires you to live in the UK. Although Alex meets all the other requirements (being under 16 and living with you), the residency requirement is a fundamental condition that you don't currently meet.

If your circumstances change and you return to live in the UK in the future, you would be able to apply for Child Benefit at that time. If you have any questions about this decision or your circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further advice.
